title: Question-writing style guide (questions-not-answers, neutral, plain-language, provenance, sensitive content)
context: Every QPL set must be authored to the same bar: questions not answers, neutral and non-leading framing, plain language at the target reading level, provenance on every framing claim, and careful handling of sensitive content (prognosis, end-of-life, fertility, genetics, cost). Without a shared style guide, different authors and reviewers will apply inconsistent standards, and agents will not know what guardrails to emit UNCERTAIN: flags for. The style guide is a prerequisite for the review rubric (qpl-rubric-001) and for authoring the pilot set (qpl-set-001).
objective: Write templates/style-guide.md — a concrete, actionable style guide for QPL question authoring covering: the questions-not-answers principle; neutrality and non-leading framing rules; plain-language target (reading level, vocabulary, sentence length); provenance requirements (every framing claim must cite an allow-listed source); sensitive content handling (prognosis/end-of-life/fertility/genetics/cost) including the mandatory verified support resource requirement; the UNCERTAIN: flag protocol for agents; the verbatim not-medical-advice disclaimer; and copyright / original-authorship rules (no copying from copyrighted QPLs).
acceptanceCriteria: templates/style-guide.md is present and covers all required sections: questions-not-answers principle, neutrality/non-leading framing, plain-language target (specific reading-level goal), provenance rules, sensitive-content handling (list each sensitivity type), UNCERTAIN: flag protocol, verbatim disclaimer text, and copyright/original-authorship rules
The style guide defines the UNCERTAIN: flag format exactly: UNCERTAIN: <location> | <type: claim|leading|advice-risk|sensitivity|source|ambiguous> | <note>
The verbatim disclaimer is quoted exactly: 'This is education, not medical advice — always consult your own care team'
At least one credentialed oncology clinician and one patient advocate have reviewed and signed off on the style guide; sign-off recorded in the PR
The guide is written in plain language itself, consistent with the standard it prescribes, and is short enough to be read in full by a contributing agent (under 2000 words)
